category_title: Resistant eleventh grader with behavioral history and workplace-centered identity
minimal_context: Derek is working on an independent reading assignment in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please go ahead and read this text independently, and let me know when you are finished with the section.

STUDENT: (Slouches in his chair and quickly flips to the end of the pages) I'm done. I finished it.

TUTOR: That was very fast. What was the passage about?

STUDENT: I don't know. My eyes just seem to skip over words as I’m going down the page.

TUTOR: You need to go back to the beginning and try reading it again so you can understand the meaning.

STUDENT: (Crosses his arms) It makes me feel like I do not want to read anymore. This is really boring. I really want to leave.

options.A: Use desk carrels to provide areas of personal space and make a clear distinction between individual and group reading.
options.B: Provide access to socially appropriate sensory stimulation during independent reading assignments, such as a squishy stress-relief ball.
options.C: Model how one reads and learns through teaching strategies in short time segments utilizing a variety of contexts.
options.D: Maintain a ratio of praise to correction at 3:1 or 4:1 during independent reading assignments in the classroom.
